deals.evidence: Le 26 janvier 2017, Michel Seydoux cède le LOSC à Gérard Lopez.
deals.headline: Michel Seydoux sells LOSC to Gérard Lopez
deals.summary: Gérard Lopez, a Spanish-Luxembourg businessman, bought LOSC from Michel Seydoux, ending more than fifteen years of the same presidency. Mediacités later reported that Lopez financed the purchase entirely with borrowed money, at least €225m in his first two years, from Elliott Management. No purchase price is stated on the cited page.

deals.evidence: sauvé par le prêt de 140 millions d’euros du fonds d’investissement Elliott
deals.headline: Elliott's €140m loan keeps Lopez-era LOSC afloat
deals.summary: Sud Ouest reports that LOSC, threatened with relegation in 2018, was saved by a €140m loan from the investment fund Elliott. Mediacités describes Lopez's ownership as a leveraged buyout financed by Elliott with at least €225m borrowed in the first two years. In December 2020 Elliott, as creditor, pushed Lopez out.

deals.evidence: La banque a racheté entre 50 et 60 millions d'euros d'obligations émises par Eliott
deals.headline: JPMorgan Chase buys €50m-60m of Elliott-issued debt tied to LOSC
deals.source_name: Europe 1 (AFP), 10 August 2018, via the Internet Archive
deals.summary: AFP reported that JPMorgan Chase bought part of the debt LOSC had contracted with Elliott: between €50m and €60m of bonds issued by Elliott. No single amount is stated, so amount is left null.

deals.evidence: transfert de propriété de la société Victory Soccer Limited, propriété de Gérard Lopez, à Callisto Sporting S.à.r.l., propriété de Merlyn Partners SCSp
deals.headline: Merlyn Partners takes over LOSC from Gérard Lopez
deals.investor: Merlyn Partners SCSp (through Callisto Sporting S.à r.l.)
deals.source_name: News Tank Sport, quoting LOSC's statement of 18 December 2020
deals.summary: LOSC announced on 18 December 2020 the completed transfer of Victory Soccer Limited, Gérard Lopez's London company that indirectly held nearly all of the club, to Callisto Sporting S.à r.l., owned by the Luxembourg fund Merlyn Partners SCSp. Olivier Létang became president. Mediacités reported that the new owners brought €40m of fresh money and a promise to cut debt sharply; the DNCG cleared the business plan on 4 January 2021. No price was disclosed.

name: LOSC Lille
notes: The earlier record's capacity (50,186, footballgroundmap) is replaced by the stadium operator's own figure, 50,000 seats in football/rugby configuration. The operator also says more than 50,100 seats were installed. Financials come from the LFP/DNCG individual club accounts for 2024/25 (k€, LOSC Lille SA + association + SCI Domaine de Luchin), a Champions League season (last 16). Player trading added 72,436 k€ to the 18,386 k€ operating result before transfers; net profit was 81,666 k€ after 19,436 k€ of tax and profit-sharing. The DNCG balance sheet shows cash of 87,179 k€ and financial debts of 6,140 k€; net debt is not stated, so it is left null. Merlyn's percentage is not published: the club's 2020 statement says Victory Soccer held 'la quasi-totalité' of LOSC. The JPMorgan row has no amount because AFP gave only a €50m-60m range; the Europe 1 original returns 403, so the archived copy is cited. The registry lists Olivier Létang as chair of the board, with Christophe Chenut, Maren Schirmer and Dawood Syed as directors. LOSC lists New Balance and Boulanger as 'partenaires principaux' but does not say which is kit supplier or shirt sponsor, so both fields are null. No valuation, attendance or social count was read on a citable page.

owners.evidence: transfert de propriété de la société Victory Soccer Limited, propriété de Gérard Lopez, à Callisto Sporting S.à.r.l., propriété de Merlyn Partners SCSp
owners.name: Merlyn Partners SCSp (through Callisto Sporting S.à r.l.)

ownership_summary: LOSC Lille SA is owned by Merlyn Partners SCSp, a Luxembourg-based investment fund, through Callisto Sporting S.à r.l. Merlyn's public faces are Alessandro Barnaba, Maarten Petermann and founder Maren Schirmer, who sits on LOSC's board. Merlyn took control in December 2020 by buying Victory Soccer Ltd, the London company through which Gérard Lopez held nearly all of the club after an Elliott-financed leveraged buyout (2017-2020). No stake percentage is published. Barnaba told the Gazzetta dello Sport in November 2024 that the fund would consider a good offer; later that month chairman and chief executive Olivier Létang said the club was not for sale. In November 2025 Le Républicain Lorrain still reported that Merlyn would sell for a good offer. No sale has been announced.
